entries.details: Keep variables containing KEY, SECRET, or TOKEN before other filters run (default: true). Set to false to apply automatic secret-name exclusions.

entries.name: shell_environment_policy.filters
entries.details: Canonical case-insensitive environment-variable pattern filters. Include entries create an allowlist and can't restore excluded values. Explicit `set` values apply after exclusions. Don't combine filters with legacy `exclude` or `include_only` arrays in the same layer.

entries.name: shell_environment_policy.exclude
entries.details: Legacy environment-variable exclusion patterns. Use `shell_environment_policy.filters` for new configuration; don't combine both forms in the same layer.

entries.name: shell_environment_policy.include_only
entries.details: Legacy allowlist of environment-variable patterns. Use `shell_environment_policy.filters` for new configuration; don't combine both forms in the same layer.

entries.name: shell_environment_policy.set
entries.details: Explicit environment values injected after exclusions; include filters can still remove them.

entries.name: shell_environment_policy.experimental_use_profile
entries.details: Use the user shell profile when spawning subprocesses.

entries.name: project_root_markers
entries.details: List of project root marker filenames; used when searching parent directories for the project root.

entries.name: project_doc_max_bytes

entries.name: project_doc_fallback_filenames

entries.name: history.persistence
entries.details: Control whether Codex saves session transcripts to history.jsonl.

entries.name: tool_output_token_limit
entries.details: Token budget for storing individual tool/function outputs in history.

entries.name: background_terminal_max_timeout
entries.details: Maximum poll window in milliseconds for empty `write_stdin` polls (background terminal polling). Default: `300000` (5 minutes). Replaces the older `background_terminal_timeout` key.

entries.name: history.max_bytes
entries.details: If set, caps the history file size in bytes by dropping oldest entries.

entries.name: file_opener

entries.name: otel.metrics_exporter

entries.name: otel.log_user_prompt

entries.details: Exporter endpoint for OTEL logs.

entries.name: otel.exporter.<id>.protocol
entries.details: Protocol used by the OTLP/HTTP exporter.

entries.name: otel.exporter.<id>.headers
entries.details: Static headers included with OTEL exporter requests.

entries.name: otel.trace_exporter.<id>.endpoint
entries.details: Trace exporter endpoint for OTEL logs.

entries.name: otel.trace_exporter.<id>.protocol
entries.details: Protocol used by the OTLP/HTTP trace exporter.

entries.name: otel.trace_exporter.<id>.headers
entries.details: Static headers included with OTEL trace exporter requests.

entries.name: otel.exporter.<id>.tls.ca-certificate
entries.details: CA certificate path for OTEL exporter TLS.

entries.name: otel.exporter.<id>.tls.client-certificate
entries.details: Client certificate path for OTEL exporter TLS.

entries.name: otel.exporter.<id>.tls.client-private-key
entries.details: Client private key path for OTEL exporter TLS.

entries.name: otel.trace_exporter.<id>.tls.ca-certificate
entries.details: CA certificate path for OTEL trace exporter TLS.

entries.name: otel.trace_exporter.<id>.tls.client-certificate
entries.details: Client certificate path for OTEL trace exporter TLS.

entries.name: otel.trace_exporter.<id>.tls.client-private-key
entries.details: Client private key path for OTEL trace exporter TLS.

entries.name: desktop.custom_file_handlers.<id>
entries.details: User-level only. Defines an additional **Open in** target for the ChatGPT desktop app. See [Add custom file handlers](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-advanced#add-custom-file-handlers) for examples and handler ID constraints.

entries.name: desktop.custom_file_handlers.<id>.label
entries.details: Display name shown in **Open in** menus. Required.

entries.name: desktop.custom_file_handlers.<id>.icon
entries.details: Bundled asset path, Base64-encoded `data:image/...` URL, file URI, or absolute local path for the handler icon. Required; unsupported sources use the default VS Code icon.

entries.name: desktop.custom_file_handlers.<id>.command
entries.details: Executable path or command name to detect and launch. Required.

entries.name: desktop.custom_file_handlers.<id>.args
entries.details: Arguments inserted between the command and file input (default: `[]`).

entries.name: desktop.custom_file_handlers.<id>.input
entries.details: How the app sends file input to the handler (default: `path`).

entries.name: desktop.custom_file_handlers.<id>.supports_ssh
entries.details: Offer the handler for files in SSH workspaces (default: `false`).

entries.name: tui
entries.details: TUI-specific options such as enabling inline desktop notifications.

entries.name: tui.notifications
entries.details: Enable TUI notifications; optionally restrict to specific event types.

entries.name: tui.notification_method
entries.details: Notification method for terminal notifications (default: auto).

entries.name: tui.notification_condition
entries.details: Control whether TUI notifications fire only when the terminal is unfocused or regardless of focus. Defaults to `unfocused`.

entries.name: tui.animations
entries.details: Enable terminal animations (welcome screen, shimmer, spinner) (default: true).

entries.name: tui.alternate_screen
entries.details: Control alternate screen usage for the TUI (default: auto; auto skips it in Zellij to preserve scrollback).

entries.name: tui.resume_cwd
entries.details: Working directory to use when resuming or forking a session. When unset, Codex asks you to choose if your current directory differs from the session's saved directory.

entries.name: tui.vim_mode_default
entries.details: Start the composer in Vim normal mode instead of insert mode (default: false). You can still toggle it per session with `/vim`.

entries.name: tui.raw_output_mode
entries.details: Start the TUI in raw scrollback mode for copy-friendly terminal selection (default: false). You can toggle it with `/raw` or the default `alt-r` key binding.

entries.name: tui.show_tooltips
entries.details: Show onboarding tooltips in the TUI welcome screen (default: true).

entries.name: tui.status_line
entries.details: Ordered list of TUI footer status-line item identifiers. `null` disables the status line.

entries.name: tui.terminal_title
tui.theme
entries.details: Syntax-highlighting theme override (kebab-case theme name).

entries.name: tui.keymap.<context>.<action>
entries.details: Keyboard shortcut binding for a TUI action. Supported contexts include `global`, `chat`, `composer`, `editor`, `vim_normal`, `vim_operator`, `vim_text_object`, `pager`, `list`, and `approval`. Selected composer actions fall back to matching `tui.keymap.global` bindings; context-specific bindings take precedence when supported.

entries.name: tui.keymap.<context>.<action> = []
entries.details: Unbind the action in that keymap context. Key names use normalized strings such as `ctrl-a`, `shift-enter`, `page-down`, or `minus`.

entries.name: marketplaces.<name>.source_type
entries.details: Source kind for a configured plugin marketplace. Marketplaces can be defined in system, cloud-managed, user, or trusted-project config.toml.

entries.name: marketplaces.<name>.source
entries.details: Git repository location or local marketplace root directory. Use an absolute path for a local source; the directory contains .agents/plugins/marketplace.json.

entries.name: marketplaces.<name>.ref
entries.details: Optional Git branch, tag, or commit for the marketplace.

entries.name: marketplaces.<name>.sparse_paths
entries.details: Optional sparse checkout paths for a Git marketplace. Include the marketplace catalog and any local plugin directories it references.

entries.name: plugins.<plugin>.enabled
entries.details: Enable or disable a local-marketplace plugin using a `plugin-name@marketplace-name` key. Read from the effective merged config; trusted-project settings can override user, cloud-managed, and system defaults. Marketplace refresh can install or refresh configured plugins even when disabled. This does not override workspace-managed enabled states.

entries.name: plugins.<plugin>.mcp_servers.<server>.enabled
entries.details: Enable or disable an MCP server bundled by an installed plugin without changing the plugin manifest.

entries.name: plugins.<plugin>.mcp_servers.<server>.default_tools_approval_mode
entries.details: Default approval behavior for tools on a plugin-provided MCP server.

entries.name: plugins.<plugin>.mcp_servers.<server>.enabled_tools
entries.details: Allow list of tools exposed from a plugin-provided MCP server.

entries.name: plugins.<plugin>.mcp_servers.<server>.disabled_tools
entries.details: Deny list applied after `enabled_tools` for a plugin-provided MCP server.

entries.name: plugins.<plugin>.mcp_servers.<server>.tools.<tool>.approval_mode
entries.details: Per-tool approval behavior override for a plugin-provided MCP tool.

entries.name: tui.model_availability_nux.<model>
entries.details: Internal startup-tooltip state keyed by model slug.

entries.name: hide_agent_reasoning
entries.details: Suppress reasoning events in both the TUI and `codex exec` output.

entries.name: show_raw_agent_reasoning
entries.details: Surface raw reasoning content when the active model emits it.

entries.name: disable_paste_burst
entries.details: Disable burst-paste detection in the TUI.

entries.name: windows_wsl_setup_acknowledged
entries.details: Track Windows onboarding acknowledgement (Windows only).

entries.name: chatgpt_base_url
entries.details: Override the base URL used during the ChatGPT login flow.

entries.name: cli_auth_credentials_store
entries.details: Control where the CLI stores cached credentials.

entries.name: mcp_oauth_credentials_store
entries.details: Preferred store for MCP OAuth credentials.

entries.name: mcp_oauth_callback_port
entries.details: Optional global fixed port for the local HTTP callback server used during MCP OAuth login. A server-specific `oauth.callback_port` takes precedence. When neither is set, Codex binds to an ephemeral port chosen by the OS.

entries.name: mcp_oauth_callback_url
entries.details: Optional base callback URL for MCP OAuth login, such as a devbox ingress URL. Newly added pre-registered clients use this URL unchanged when the authorization server supports issuer identification; existing clients without a saved callback append a server-specific callback ID. Without issuer support, any pre-registered MCP server whose configured callback lacks the required ID falls back to this URL with the ID appended. Callback URL ports don't select the listener port.

entries.name: experimental_use_unified_exec_tool
entries.details: Legacy name for enabling unified exec; prefer `[features].unified_exec` or `codex --enable unified_exec`.

entries.name: tools.web_search
entries.details: Optional web search tool configuration. The object form can set search context size, allowed search domains, and approximate user location. These search-domain filters are separate from sandboxed-command network domain rules and do not restrict connectors or MCP servers.

entries.name: tools.view_image
entries.details: Enable the local-image attachment tool `view_image`.

entries.name: web_search
default_permissions
entries.details: Name of the default permissions profile to apply to sandboxed tool calls. Built-ins are `:read-only`, `:workspace`, and `:danger-full-access`; custom profile names require matching `[permissions.<name>]` tables. Don't combine with `sandbox_mode` or `[sandbox_workspace_write]`.

entries.name: permissions.<name>.description
entries.details: Human-readable description for this named profile. A profile does not inherit its parent's description through `extends`.

entries.name: permissions.<name>.extends
entries.details: Optional parent profile applied before this named profile. Set it to another named profile, `:read-only`, or `:workspace`; `:danger-full-access`, undefined parents, and cycles are rejected.

entries.name: permissions.<name>.workspace_roots
entries.details: Profile-defined workspace roots that receive `:workspace_roots` filesystem rules alongside the session's runtime workspace roots.

entries.name: permissions.<name>.workspace_roots.<path>
entries.details: Opt a path into the profile's workspace root set when `true`. Disabled entries remain inactive.

entries.name: permissions.<name>.filesystem
entries.details: Named filesystem permission profile. Each key is an absolute path or special token such as `:minimal` or `:workspace_roots`.

entries.name: permissions.<name>.filesystem.glob_scan_max_depth
entries.details: Maximum depth for expanding deny-read glob patterns on platforms that snapshot matches before sandbox startup. Must be at least `1` when set.

entries.name: permissions.<name>.filesystem.<path-or-glob>
permissions.<name>.network.enabled
entries.details: Enable network access for commands in this permission profile. This does not start the network proxy. Without `features.network_proxy` or enabled administrator-managed networking requirements, command network access is direct and profile domain rules are not enforced.

entries.name: permissions.<name>.network.proxy_url
entries.details: HTTP listener URL used when this permissions profile enables sandboxed networking.

entries.name: permissions.<name>.network.enable_socks5
entries.details: Expose SOCKS5 support when this permissions profile enables sandboxed networking.

entries.name: permissions.<name>.network.socks_url
entries.details: SOCKS5 proxy endpoint used by this permissions profile.

entries.name: permissions.<name>.network.enable_socks5_udp
entries.details: Allow UDP over the SOCKS5 listener when enabled.

entries.name: permissions.<name>.network.allow_upstream_proxy
entries.details: Allow sandboxed networking to chain through another upstream proxy.

entries.name: permissions.<name>.network.dangerously_allow_non_loopback_proxy
entries.details: Permit non-loopback bind addresses for sandboxed networking listeners. Enabling it can expose listeners beyond localhost.

entries.name: permissions.<name>.network.dangerously_allow_all_unix_sockets
entries.details: Allow arbitrary Unix socket destinations instead of the default restricted set. Use only in tightly controlled environments.

entries.name: permissions.<name>.network.mode
entries.details: Network proxy mode used for subprocess traffic.

entries.name: permissions.<name>.network.domains
entries.details: Domain rules for sandboxed commands. Enforced only when `features.network_proxy` or enabled administrator-managed networking requirements activate the proxy. Supports exact hosts, `*.example.com`, `**.example.com`, and global `*` allow rules; `deny` wins. Does not restrict web search, apps, or MCP servers.

entries.name: permissions.<name>.network.domains.<pattern>
entries.details: Allow or deny an exact host or scoped wildcard pattern such as `*.example.com` or `**.example.com`.

entries.name: permissions.<name>.network.unix_sockets
entries.details: Unix socket allowlist overrides for sandboxed networking. Use socket paths as keys; `allow` adds a path, and `deny` rejects it.

entries.name: permissions.<name>.network.unix_sockets.<path>
entries.details: Add an absolute Unix socket path to the effective allowlist with `allow`, or reject it with `deny`. Denied entries are omitted from the effective allowlist.

entries.name: permissions.<name>.network.allow_local_binding
entries.details: Permit broader local/private-network access through sandboxed networking. Exact local IP literal or `localhost` allow rules can still permit specific local targets when this stays `false`.

entries.name: projects.<path>.trust_level
notice.hide_full_access_warning
entries.details: Track acknowledgement of the full access warning prompt.

entries.name: notice.hide_world_writable_warning
entries.details: Track acknowledgement of the Windows world-writable directories warning.

entries.name: notice.hide_rate_limit_model_nudge
entries.details: Track opt-out of the rate limit model switch reminder.

entries.name: notice.hide_gpt5_1_migration_prompt
entries.details: Track acknowledgement of the GPT-5.1 migration prompt.

entries.name: notice.hide_gpt-5.1-codex-max_migration_prompt
entries.details: Track acknowledgement of the gpt-5.1-codex-max migration prompt.

entries.name: notice.model_migrations
entries.details: Track acknowledged model migrations as old->new mappings.

entries.name: forced_login_method
entries.details: Restrict Codex to a specific authentication method.

entries.name: forced_chatgpt_workspace_id
entries.details: Limit ChatGPT logins to a specific workspace identifier.

entries.name: sqlite_home
entries.details: Enforce the directory where Codex stores SQLite-backed runtime state.

entries.name: log_dir
entries.details: Enforce the directory where Codex writes local log files.

entries.name: model_catalog_json
entries.details: Enforce the JSON model catalog Codex uses at startup.

entries.name: check_for_update_on_startup
entries.details: Enforce whether Codex checks for updates when it starts.

entries.name: allow_login_shell
entries.details: Enforce whether shell tools can start a login shell.

entries.name: allowed_login_methods
entries.details: Allow `chatgpt`, `api`, or both. If omitted, this setting doesn't restrict login methods. If set, the list must contain at least one method. `api` permits API authentication, including Amazon Bedrock. Set through the local system requirements file or macOS MDM. Cloud-managed values are ignored.

entries.name: allowed_chatgpt_workspaces
entries.details: Restrict ChatGPT login, including Codex access tokens, to the listed workspace IDs. An empty list disables ChatGPT login; API authentication remains available when permitted. Set through the local system requirements file or macOS MDM; cloud-managed values are ignored.

entries.name: cli_auth_credentials_store
entries.details: Enforce the CLI credential store before authentication loads. `file` uses `CODEX_HOME/auth.json`; `keyring` requires the OS credential store; `auto` falls back to a file if the credential store is unavailable; `ephemeral` keeps credentials in memory for the current process. Set through the local system requirements file or macOS MDM; cloud-managed values are ignored.

entries.name: chatgpt_base_url
entries.details: Enforce the ChatGPT service base URL before authentication and cloud-policy retrieval. This doesn't configure every Codex network destination. Set through the local system requirements file or macOS MDM; cloud-managed values are ignored.

entries.name: feedback
entries.details: Managed feedback settings.

entries.name: feedback.enabled
entries.details: Enforce whether users can submit feedback across Codex clients.

entries.name: allowed_approval_policies
entries.details: Allowed approval policies, such as `on-request`, `never`, and `granular`. Include `untrusted` to permit the stricter policy derived from an untrusted project; it cannot be selected directly with `approval_policy`.

entries.name: allowed_approvals_reviewers
entries.details: Allowed values for `approvals_reviewer`, such as `user` and `auto_review`.

entries.name: guardian_policy_config
entries.details: Managed Markdown policy instructions for automatic review. This takes precedence over local `[auto_review].policy`. Blank values are ignored.

entries.name: allowed_permission_profiles
entries.details: Complete list of allowed permission profiles. Profiles set to `true` are allowed. Profiles that are omitted or set to `false` are denied, including profiles added in future versions. When requirements sources are combined, entries are matched by profile name.

entries.name: allowed_permission_profiles.<name>
entries.details: Allow or deny a built-in or custom permission profile defined in a loaded config or requirements source. A later, higher-precedence requirements source can use `false` to turn off a profile allowed by an earlier, lower-precedence source.

entries.name: default_permissions
entries.details: Managed default permission profile. The profile must be allowed by `allowed_permission_profiles`. Set this explicitly for predictable behavior; if omitted, Codex defaults to `:workspace` only when both `:workspace` and `:read-only` are explicitly allowed.

entries.name: enforce_residency
entries.details: Require Codex service traffic to use a supported data residency. Currently accepts `us`.

entries.name: models
entries.details: Managed model defaults for new threads. These values take priority over user and project defaults, but an explicit selection for the new thread can override them.

entries.name: models.new_thread
entries.details: Defaults to apply when a new local thread starts. Each model setting is optional.

entries.name: models.new_thread.model
entries.details: Default model for new threads. An explicit `--model` or model/reasoning `--config` override takes precedence.

entries.name: models.new_thread.model_reasoning_effort
entries.details: Default reasoning effort for new threads. An explicit model or reasoning-effort override skips both managed model fields.

entries.name: models.new_thread.service_tier
entries.details: Default service tier for new threads. An explicit service-tier override takes precedence independently of the model fields.

entries.name: permissions
entries.details: Admin-defined permission profiles keyed by profile name. Uses the same profile fields as `config.toml`.

entries.name: permissions.<name>
entries.details: Admin-defined permission profile. The name can't start with `:`, use the reserved name `filesystem`, or duplicate a profile from a loaded config. Uses the same profile fields as `config.toml`; see the Permissions guide for the complete profile schema.

entries.name: allowed_sandbox_modes
entries.details: Allowed values for `sandbox_mode`.

entries.name: windows
entries.details: Native Windows sandbox requirements.

entries.name: windows.allowed_sandbox_implementations
entries.details: Allowed native Windows sandbox implementations for `windows.sandbox` (`elevated` and `unelevated`). The list must not be empty. When both are allowed and no mode is selected, Codex prefers `elevated`.

entries.name: windows.sandbox_private_desktop
entries.details: Enforce whether the native Windows sandbox starts its child process on a private desktop.

entries.name: remote_sandbox_config
entries.details: Host-specific sandbox requirements. The first entry whose `hostname_patterns` match the resolved host name overrides top-level `allowed_sandbox_modes` for that requirements source. Host-specific entries currently override sandbox modes only.

entries.name: remote_sandbox_config[].hostname_patterns
entries.details: Case-insensitive host name patterns. Supports `*` for any sequence of characters and `?` for one character.

entries.name: remote_sandbox_config[].allowed_sandbox_modes
entries.details: Allowed sandbox modes to apply when this host-specific entry matches.

entries.name: allowed_web_search_modes
entries.details: Allowed values for `web_search` (`disabled`, `cached`, `indexed`, `live`). `disabled` is always allowed; an empty list effectively allows only `disabled`.

entries.name: allow_managed_hooks_only
entries.details: When `true`, Codex skips user, project, session, and plugin hooks while still allowing managed hooks from `requirements.toml` and other managed config layers.

entries.name: allow_appshots
entries.details: Set to `false` to disable Appshots for managed users. If omitted, Appshots remain unconstrained by requirements and follow normal product availability.

entries.name: allow_remote_control
entries.details: Set to `false` to disable device remote control for managed users. If omitted, device remote control remains unconstrained by requirements and follows normal product availability.

entries.name: allow_browser_and_computer_use
entries.details: Set to `false` to block both agent-driven Browser Use and native-app Computer Use. Setting it to `true` or omitting it does not enable either feature; the remaining feature, policy, and approval checks still apply.

entries.name: features.plugin_sharing
entries.details: Set to `false` in cloud-managed `requirements.toml` to disable workspace sharing for locally built plugins.

entries.name: features
entries.details: Pinned feature values. Use canonical names from `config.toml` for runtime features; documented app-only requirement keys are also supported here.

entries.name: features.<name>
entries.details: Require a documented runtime or app feature to stay enabled or disabled.

entries.name: features.apps
entries.details: Pin Apps integration availability on or off for managed users.

entries.name: features.in_app_updates
entries.details: Set to `false` in `requirements.toml` to disable in-app updates. Updates remain enabled by default when this requirement is omitted.

entries.name: features.in_app_browser
entries.details: Set to `false` in `requirements.toml` to disable the built-in browser pane that users open and control directly.

entries.name: features.browser_use
entries.details: Set to `false` in `requirements.toml` to disable agent-driven Browser Use.

entries.name: features.browser_use_external
entries.details: Set to `false` in `requirements.toml` to prevent Codex from operating supported browsers through the ChatGPT browser extension, including existing tabs and signed-in sessions.

entries.name: features.browser_use_full_cdp_access
entries.details: Set to `false` in `requirements.toml` to disable full Chrome DevTools Protocol access in the local runtime, including Browser Developer mode, and prevent the ChatGPT desktop app from enabling the corresponding setting. If omitted, normal product availability applies.

entries.name: features.fast_mode
entries.details: Pin the canonical `fast_mode` feature on or off for managed users.

entries.name: features.guardian_approval
entries.details: Pin Guardian approval availability on or off for managed users.

entries.name: features.memories
entries.details: Pin Memories availability on or off for managed users.

entries.name: features.multi_agent
entries.details: Pin multi-agent availability on or off for managed users.

entries.name: features.plugins
entries.details: Pin plugin availability on or off for managed users.

entries.name: features.remote_plugin
entries.details: Pin remote plugin catalog availability on or off for managed users.

entries.name: features.computer_use
entries.details: Set to `false` in `requirements.toml` to disable Computer Use, Record & Replay, and related install or enablement flows.

entries.name: features.workspace_dependencies
entries.details: Pin bundled workspace-dependency runtime availability on or off for managed users.

entries.name: in_app_browser
entries.details: Requirements for the built-in browser pane. These settings do not control agent-driven Browser Use.

entries.name: in_app_browser.allow_external_browser_settings_import
entries.details: Set to `false` to prevent users from importing settings or browsing data from an external browser into the built-in browser. Setting it to `true` or omitting it leaves the import available when other product checks allow it. This is a managed-only setting with no `config.toml` override.

entries.name: browser_use
entries.details: Managed requirements for agent-driven Browser Use.

entries.name: browser_use.allow_history_access
entries.details: Set to `false` to prevent Browser Use from reading browser history. Setting it to `true` or omitting it leaves normal history settings and availability checks in place.

entries.name: browser_use.disable_auto_review
entries.details: Set to `true` to skip automatic review for Browser Use and ask the user for approval instead. Setting it to `false` or omitting it leaves automatic review available when other settings allow it.

entries.name: browser_use.allow_global_persistent_approval
entries.details: Set to `false` to prevent Browser Use from creating or honoring `Always allow` approvals that cover every site, such as allowing downloads from any site. Existing saved approvals are ignored, not deleted. Setting it to `true` or omitting it does not create an approval.

entries.name: browser_use.default_origin_policy
entries.details: Fallback for each Browser Use setting when no matching entry under `browser_use.origins` defines it. A matching origin rule replaces the fallback for that source. Codex then applies the stricter result from managed requirements and user configuration.

entries.name: browser_use.default_origin_policy.access
entries.details: Use `deny` to block Browser Use on origins that use the fallback. A denied origin also blocks uploads, downloads, full browser debugging access, and automatic review there. `allow` only lets normal approval and policy checks continue.

entries.name: browser_use.default_origin_policy.downloads
entries.details: Use `deny` to block Browser Use downloads on origins that use the fallback. `allow` only lets normal approval and policy checks continue.

entries.name: browser_use.default_origin_policy.uploads
entries.details: Use `deny` to block Browser Use uploads on origins that use the fallback. `allow` only lets normal approval and policy checks continue.

entries.name: browser_use.default_origin_policy.full_cdp_access
entries.details: Use `deny` to block full Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) access on origins that use the fallback. `allow` only lets normal opt-in and approval checks continue.

entries.name: browser_use.default_origin_policy.auto_review
entries.details: Use `deny` to skip automatic review on origins that use the fallback and ask the user for approval instead. `allow` leaves automatic review available when other settings allow it.

entries.name: browser_use.default_origin_policy.persistent_approval
entries.details: Set to `false` to prevent Browser Use from saving or honoring an `Always allow` approval on origins that use the fallback. Approvals for the current turn or thread can still apply. `true` makes `Always allow` available when otherwise permitted but does not create an approval.

entries.name: browser_use.default_origin_policy.access_approval_lifetime
entries.details: Set how long a non-persistent site-access approval lasts: `turn` limits it to the current turn, and `thread` keeps it for the rest of the current thread. `persistent_approval` separately controls whether `Always allow` is available. The product default is `thread`.

entries.name: browser_use.origins
browser_use.origins.<pattern>
entries.details: Policy for origins matching this pattern. If several patterns match, Codex uses the most restrictive value for each capability: `deny` over `allow`, `false` over `true`, and `turn` over `thread`.

entries.name: browser_use.origins.<pattern>.access
entries.details: Use `deny` to block Browser Use on matching origins. Denial also blocks uploads, downloads, full browser debugging access, and automatic review there. `allow` only lets normal approval and policy checks continue.

entries.name: browser_use.origins.<pattern>.downloads
entries.details: Use `deny` to block Browser Use downloads on matching origins. `allow` only lets normal approval and policy checks continue.

entries.name: browser_use.origins.<pattern>.uploads
entries.details: Use `deny` to block Browser Use uploads on matching origins. `allow` only lets normal approval and policy checks continue.

entries.name: browser_use.origins.<pattern>.full_cdp_access
entries.details: Use `deny` to block full Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) access on matching origins. `allow` only lets normal opt-in and approval checks continue.

entries.name: browser_use.origins.<pattern>.auto_review
entries.details: Use `deny` to skip automatic review on matching origins and ask the user for approval instead. `allow` leaves automatic review available when other settings allow it.

entries.name: browser_use.origins.<pattern>.persistent_approval
entries.details: Set to `false` to prevent Browser Use from saving or honoring an `Always allow` approval on matching origins. Approvals for the current turn or thread can still apply. `true` makes `Always allow` available when otherwise permitted but does not create an approval.

entries.name: browser_use.origins.<pattern>.access_approval_lifetime
entries.details: Set how long a non-persistent site-access approval for matching origins lasts: `turn` limits it to the current turn, and `thread` keeps it for the rest of the current thread. `persistent_approval` separately controls whether `Always allow` is available.

entries.name: computer_use
entries.details: Managed requirements for agent-driven work in native desktop apps. Managed app rules and `config.toml` app rules are both enforced; an app must be allowed by each policy source.

entries.name: computer_use.allow_locked_computer_use
entries.details: Set to `false` to prevent users from enabling Locked Use on a managed macOS device. This requirement removes the enablement controls; it does not turn off Locked Use if it is already enabled. If omitted, normal product availability applies.

entries.name: computer_use.allow_persistent_approval
entries.details: Set to `false` to remove the option to save app approvals across sessions. Approvals for the current session remain available. Setting it to `true` or omitting it does not approve an app.

entries.name: computer_use.default_app_access
entries.details: Fallback access for native apps that do not match a platform-specific rule. `deny` blocks access. `allow` only lets normal approval and policy checks continue. The product default is `allow`.

entries.name: computer_use.macos
entries.details: Computer Use app rules for macOS.

entries.name: computer_use.macos.bundle_ids
entries.details: Map exact macOS bundle identifiers to `allow` or `deny`. A matching rule replaces `computer_use.default_app_access` within the same policy source. A deny from either managed requirements or user configuration still blocks access.

entries.name: computer_use.macos.bundle_ids.<bundle-id>
entries.details: Use `deny` to block the exact bundle identifier. `allow` overrides only this policy source's default and still requires any other policy source and the normal approval flow to allow the app.

entries.name: computer_use.windows
entries.details: Computer Use app rules for packaged and unpackaged Windows apps.

entries.name: computer_use.windows.aumids
entries.details: Map exact, registered Application User Model IDs (AUMIDs) for signed packaged apps to `allow` or `deny`. A matching rule replaces `computer_use.default_app_access` within the same policy source.

entries.name: computer_use.windows.aumids.<aumid>
entries.details: Use `deny` to block the exact packaged-app identity. `allow` overrides only this policy source's default and still requires any other policy source and the normal approval flow to allow the app.

entries.name: computer_use.windows.exes
entries.details: Rules for signed, unpackaged Windows executables. Rules match the executable's verified publisher and signed version information, not its path or current file name. A matching deny takes precedence over matching allows. Unsigned executables use `computer_use.default_app_access`; executables whose signed identity cannot be verified unambiguously are blocked.

entries.name: computer_use.windows.exes[].publisher_name
entries.details: Required exact publisher name from the executable's trusted signing certificate, formatted as a Windows X.500 distinguished name.

entries.name: computer_use.windows.exes[].product_name
entries.details: Required exact `ProductName` from the executable's signed version information.

entries.name: computer_use.windows.exes[].binary_name
entries.details: Optional `OriginalFilename` from the executable's signed version information. Matching is case-insensitive. If a matching publisher and product rule requires this value but the executable does not provide it, Computer Use blocks the executable.

entries.name: computer_use.windows.exes[].access
entries.details: Required access decision for matching executables. `deny` blocks access. `allow` overrides only this policy source's default and still requires any other policy source and the normal approval flow to allow the app.

entries.name: experimental_network
entries.details: Administrator-managed network requirements for sandboxed local commands, enforced from `requirements.toml`. When enabled, these requirements can start the command network proxy without `features.network_proxy`. Browser tools separately check managed network denies and exclusive allowlists. These requirements do not route browser traffic through the proxy or control web search, apps, MCP servers, native-app traffic, or Codex cloud networking.

entries.name: experimental_network.enabled
entries.details: Enable sandboxed networking requirements. This does not grant network access when the active sandbox keeps command networking off.

entries.name: experimental_network.http_port
entries.details: Loopback HTTP listener port to use for `[experimental_network]` requirements.

entries.name: experimental_network.socks_port
entries.details: Loopback SOCKS5 listener port to use for `[experimental_network]` requirements.

entries.name: experimental_network.allow_upstream_proxy
entries.details: Allow sandboxed networking to chain through an upstream proxy from the environment.

entries.name: experimental_network.dangerously_allow_non_loopback_proxy
entries.details: Permit non-loopback listener addresses for `[experimental_network]` requirements. Enabling it can expose listeners beyond localhost.

entries.name: experimental_network.dangerously_allow_all_unix_sockets
entries.details: Permit arbitrary Unix socket destinations instead of allowlist-only access. Use only in tightly controlled environments.

entries.name: experimental_network.domains
entries.details: Map-shaped administrator domain policy for sandboxed networking. Supports exact hosts, `*.example.com` for subdomains only, `**.example.com` for apex plus subdomains, and global `*` allow rules; prefer scoped rules because `*` broadly opens public outbound access. `deny` wins on conflicts. Do not combine this with `experimental_network.allowed_domains` or `experimental_network.denied_domains`.

entries.name: experimental_network.allowed_domains
entries.details: Administrator allow rules for sandboxed-command networking while the managed network proxy is enabled. These rules do not apply to web search, apps, or MCP servers. Do not combine this with `experimental_network.domains`.

entries.name: experimental_network.denied_domains
entries.details: List-shaped administrator deny rules for sandboxed networking. Do not combine this with `experimental_network.domains`.

entries.name: experimental_network.managed_allowed_domains_only
entries.details: When `true`, only administrator-managed allow rules remain effective while sandboxed networking requirements are active; user allowlist additions are ignored. Without managed allow rules, user-added domain allow rules do not remain effective.

entries.name: experimental_network.unix_sockets
entries.details: Administrator-managed Unix socket policy for sandboxed networking.

entries.name: experimental_network.allow_local_binding
entries.details: Permit broader local/private-network access for sandboxed networking. Exact local IP literal or `localhost` allow rules can still permit specific local targets when this stays `false`.

entries.name: hooks
entries.details: Admin-enforced managed lifecycle hooks. Requires a managed hook directory and uses the same event schema as inline `[hooks]` in `config.toml`.

entries.name: hooks.managed_dir
entries.details: Directory containing managed hook scripts on macOS and Linux. Codex validates that it is absolute and exists before loading managed hooks.

entries.name: hooks.windows_managed_dir
entries.details: Directory containing managed hook scripts on Windows. Codex validates that it is absolute and exists before loading managed hooks.

entries.name: hooks.<Event>
entries.details: Matcher groups for a hook event such as `PreToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `PostToolUse`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, `UserPromptSubmit`, or `Stop`.

entries.name: hooks.<Event>[].hooks
entries.details: Hook handlers for a matcher group. Command and MCP tool hooks are supported while prompt and agent hook handlers are parsed but skipped.

entries.name: hooks.<Event>[].hooks[].async
entries.details: Run a command hook in the background without delaying the triggering operation. Defaults to `false`; `SessionEnd` always runs synchronously. See [Run hooks in the background](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks#run-hooks-in-the-background).

entries.name: hooks.<Event>[].hooks[].additionalContextLimit
entries.details: Approximate per-handler token threshold for saving oversized `additionalContext` to disk and showing the model a shorter preview. Defaults to `2500`; `0` passes the full context directly to the model. See [Large hook output](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks#large-hook-output).

entries.name: hooks.<Event>[].hooks[].commandWindows
entries.details: Windows-only command override for command hooks. The TOML alias `command_windows` is also accepted.

entries.name: permissions.filesystem.deny_read
entries.details: Admin-enforced filesystem read denials. Entries can be paths or glob patterns, and users cannot weaken them with local config.

entries.name: mcp_servers
entries.details: Allowlist of MCP servers that may be enabled. Both the server name (`<id>`) and its identity must match for the MCP server to be enabled. Any configured MCP server not in the allowlist (or with a mismatched identity) is disabled.

entries.name: mcp_servers.<id>.identity
entries.details: Identity rule for a single MCP server. Set either `command` (stdio) or `url` (streamable HTTP).

entries.name: mcp_servers.<id>.identity.command
entries.details: Allow an MCP stdio server by exact command string, or use a matcher table to require an exact executable and ordered argument matchers. The string form doesn't inspect arguments, `cwd`, `env`, or `env_vars`.

entries.name: mcp_servers.<id>.identity.command.executable
entries.details: Executable that the stdio server's configured `command` must match exactly.

entries.name: mcp_servers.<id>.identity.command.args
entries.details: Ordered argument matchers for a stdio server. The configured argument list must have the same length, and every position must match. Command matchers don't inspect `cwd`, `env`, or `env_vars`.

entries.name: mcp_servers.<id>.identity.command.args[].match
entries.details: Match operation for this argument position.

entries.name: mcp_servers.<id>.identity.command.args[].value
entries.details: Value used by an `exact` or `prefix` argument matcher.

entries.name: mcp_servers.<id>.identity.command.args[].expression
entries.details: Regular expression used by a `regex` argument matcher. The expression must be valid and match the complete argument value.

entries.name: mcp_servers.<id>.identity.url
entries.details: Allow an MCP streamable HTTP server by exact URL string, or use an `exact`, `prefix`, or `regex` value matcher table.

entries.name: mcp_servers.<id>.identity.url.match
entries.details: Match operation for the configured MCP server URL.

entries.name: mcp_servers.<id>.identity.url.value
entries.details: Value used by an `exact` or `prefix` URL matcher.

entries.name: mcp_servers.<id>.identity.url.expression
entries.details: Regular expression used by a `regex` URL matcher. The expression must be valid and match the complete URL value.

entries.name: plugins
entries.details: Plugin-specific MCP server allowlists keyed by plugin identifier. When this table is present, plugin-bundled servers without a matching plugin and server entry are disabled.

entries.name: plugins.<plugin>.mcp_servers
entries.details: Allowlist for MCP servers bundled with one plugin. Plugin server requirements use the same exact identity and matcher forms as top-level `mcp_servers` requirements.

entries.name: plugins.<plugin>.mcp_servers.<server>.identity
entries.details: Identity rule for one plugin-bundled MCP server. Set either `command` (stdio) or `url` (streamable HTTP).

entries.name: plugins.<plugin>.mcp_servers.<server>.identity.command
entries.details: Allow a plugin's stdio MCP server by exact command string, or use a matcher table to require an exact executable and ordered argument matchers.

entries.name: plugins.<plugin>.mcp_servers.<server>.identity.command.executable
entries.details: Executable that the plugin-bundled stdio server's configured command must match exactly.

entries.name: plugins.<plugin>.mcp_servers.<server>.identity.command.args
entries.details: Ordered argument matchers for a plugin-bundled stdio server. The configured argument list must have the same length, and every position must match.

entries.name: plugins.<plugin>.mcp_servers.<server>.identity.command.args[].match
entries.details: Match operation for this argument position.

entries.name: plugins.<plugin>.mcp_servers.<server>.identity.command.args[].value
entries.details: Value used by an `exact` or `prefix` argument matcher.

entries.name: plugins.<plugin>.mcp_servers.<server>.identity.command.args[].expression
entries.details: Regular expression used by a `regex` argument matcher. The expression must match the complete argument value.

entries.name: plugins.<plugin>.mcp_servers.<server>.identity.url
entries.details: Allow a plugin's streamable HTTP MCP server by exact URL string, or use an `exact`, `prefix`, or `regex` value matcher table.

entries.name: plugins.<plugin>.mcp_servers.<server>.identity.url.match
entries.details: Match operation for the plugin-bundled MCP server URL.

entries.name: plugins.<plugin>.mcp_servers.<server>.identity.url.value
entries.details: Value used by an `exact` or `prefix` URL matcher.

entries.name: plugins.<plugin>.mcp_servers.<server>.identity.url.expression
entries.details: Regular expression used by a `regex` URL matcher. The expression must match the complete URL value.

entries.name: marketplaces
entries.details: Admin requirements for plugin marketplace sources. Rules take effect when `restrict_to_allowed_sources` is `true`.

entries.name: marketplaces.restrict_to_allowed_sources
entries.details: When `true`, require configured marketplace sources to match `allowed_sources` for marketplace add, plugin install, refresh, and runtime loading. OpenAI-curated Git catalogs, including the API-key catalog, must also match the allowlist. Bundled and remotely installed workspace plugins are separate from this curated Git source policy.

entries.name: marketplaces.allowed_sources
entries.details: Allowed marketplace sources keyed by administrator-chosen rule name. Distinct names accumulate across requirements layers; fields under the same name use normal layer precedence.

entries.name: marketplaces.allowed_sources.<name>
entries.details: One allowed source rule. The final `source` value after requirements merge determines which sibling fields Codex interprets.

entries.name: marketplaces.allowed_sources.<name>.source
entries.details: Marketplace source matcher type. Use `git` for one repository, `host_pattern` for Git hosts matched by regular expression, or `local` for one directory.

entries.name: marketplaces.allowed_sources.<name>.url
marketplaces.allowed_sources.<name>.ref
entries.details: Optional exact Git ref for a `git` rule. When omitted, the rule allows any ref for the matching repository.

entries.name: marketplaces.allowed_sources.<name>.host_pattern
marketplaces.allowed_sources.<name>.path
apps

entries.name: apps.<id>.tools.<tool>.approval_mode

entries.name: rules

entries.name: rules.prefix_rules[].pattern

entries.name: rules.prefix_rules[].pattern[].token

entries.name: rules.prefix_rules[].pattern[].any_of

entries.name: rules.prefix_rules[].decision

entries.name: rules.prefix_rules[].justification

entries.details: Type a lone `$` at the prompt and press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to hand the terminal over to a real interactive shell (`$SHELL` on Unix, `%COMSPEC%` on Windows) rooted at the session's working directory. entries.name: `/autopilot [OBJECTIVE]`, `/goal [OBJECTIVE]`
entries.details: Start or refocus autopilot mode, optionally with an explicit objective (for example, `/goal Refactor the auth module`). Without an objective, autopilot infers intent from context, and the status panel shows your last prompt as the inferred objective. You can cap AI-credit spend for the objective by using `--max-ai-credits N` (for example, `/goal Refactor the auth module --max-ai-credits 5`). When the cap is reached, autopilot pauses and opens a panel reporting credits used against the cap. Enter a new amount to resume with a fresh credit window, or dismiss the panel to stay paused. You can also resume a paused objective yourself, without the panel, by running the option on its own with no objective text—for example, `/goal --max-ai-credits 5`. This is the same action the panel performs: it opens a fresh window of the credits you specify (the full new cap, not an increment) and continues the objective. `/goal on` and `/goal off` toggle autopilot mode without setting an objective and don't accept `--max-ai-credits`. An active goal renders as a pinned panel above the composer, showing the objective, credits used, and todo progress. The panel auto-collapses to a single identity row on short terminals (below 30 rows) and expands above that threshold; press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>X</kbd> then `g` to override the automatic sizing by hand.

A model with vendor-specific data retention terms shows a data retention warning banner with a link to the vendor's policy. Usable mid-turn: a change requested while the agent is running is queued as a cancellable (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd>) command and applied once the current turn finishes, instead of switching the live model mid-request. entries.name: `/move [branch\|task]`
entries.details: Move uncommitted changes into a new Git worktree and switch to it. Pass a branch name, a task description (multiline supported, used as the opening prompt in the new worktree), or omit the argument to auto-generate a branch name from the conversation. Requires a Git repository. Only available in experimental mode.

entries.name: `--add-dir=PATH`

entries.name: `-r`, `--resume[=VALUE]`
entries.details: Resume a previous interactive session by choosing from a list. Optionally specify a session ID, ID prefix, or session name. Name matching is exact and case-insensitive; falls back to the auto-generated summary when no explicit name matches. Conflicts with `--continue`. Bare `--resume` (no value) shows an interactive session picker, which requires a TTY. If multiple sessions exist and the picker can't be shown (for example under `-p`, a non-TTY `-i`, or piped stdin), the CLI exits with an error instead of silently starting a new session—pass an explicit `--resume=SESSION-ID` or use `--continue`. |

entries.name: `--session-id ID`
entries.details: Use an exact session or task ID when you do not want `--resume`'s broader matching by ID prefix or session name. If the ID matches an existing session or task, that session or task is resumed. If nothing matches, a new session is created only when the value is a valid UUID. Names and ID prefixes do not create new sessions. Do not combine this option with other session-selection or session-starting options such as `--resume`, `--continue`, or `--connect`, because they compete to decide which session to open or create. |

entries.details: Set to `1` or `true` to opt into HTTP/2 transport. HTTP/1.1 is the default.

Disabling bypass or credential injection cannot be re-enabled. Filesystem allow lists can only be narrowed, and denied paths can only be added to. `failIfUnavailable` can only be set by an administrator and blocks the session when the sandbox cannot be established. For the settings users can set themselves, see [User settings](#user-settings-copilotsettingsjson) or run `copilot help sandbox`.

entries.name: `default_permissions`
entries.details: String profile name | None | Names the permissions profile Codex applies by default. It must match a profile under `[permissions]` or a built-in such as `:workspace`. Set it explicitly for predictable behavior; managed requirements may omit it only when both `:workspace` and `:read-only` are explicitly allowed. Codex uses older sandbox settings unless managed `allowed_permission_profiles` tells it to use permission profiles in this setup.

entries.name: `[permissions.<name>]`
entries.details: Table | None | Defines a named profile. `default_permissions` selects one profile as the default; other permission-profile settings also use the profile name.

entries.name: `permissions.<name>.description`
entries.details: String | None | Provides a human-readable description for the profile. A profile does not inherit its parent's description through `extends`.

entries.name: `permissions.<name>.extends`
entries.details: String profile name | None | Starts this profile from another named profile or the built-in `:read-only` or `:workspace` profile. Codex rejects `:danger-full-access`, unknown parents, and inheritance cycles.

entries.name: `[permissions.<name>.workspace_roots]`
entries.details: Table | None | Adds profile-defined workspace roots that receive `:workspace_roots` filesystem rules alongside the current session's runtime workspace roots.

entries.name: `permissions.<name>.workspace_roots."<path>"`
entries.details: Boolean | `false` | Adds the path to the profile's workspace root set when `true`. Entries set to `false` remain inactive.

entries.name: `[permissions.<name>.filesystem]`
entries.details: Table | None | Maps filesystem paths to access values or scoped subpath maps. Missing or empty filesystem tables keep filesystem access restricted and emit a startup warning.

entries.name: `permissions.<name>.filesystem.glob_scan_max_depth`
entries.details: Number | None | Limits deny-read glob expansion on Linux, WSL, and native Windows when Codex snapshots matches before sandbox startup. Larger values can increase startup scanning work. Use a value of at least `1` when an unbounded `**` pattern needs bounded pre-expansion.

entries.name: `[permissions.<name>.filesystem]."<path>"`
entries.details: `read`, `write`, or `deny` | None | Grants direct access for a supported path. `deny` denies access and wins over equally specific `write` or `read` entries. Codex rejects direct write rules that the active runtime cannot enforce.

entries.name: `[permissions.<name>.filesystem."<path>"]."<subpath>"`
entries.details: `read`, `write`, or `deny` | None | Grants access to a descendant of `<path>`. Use `.` for the base path. Other subpaths must be relative descendants and cannot contain `.` or `..` components.

entries.name: `[permissions.<name>.network]`
entries.details: Table | None | Configures command network access and the policy that an active network proxy enforces. Enable `features.network_proxy` unless administrator-managed network requirements start the proxy.

entries.name: `permissions.<name>.network.enabled`
entries.details: Boolean | `false` | Enables network access for commands in the profile. It does not start the network proxy; without an active proxy, commands can connect directly without domain restrictions.

entries.name: `[permissions.<name>.network.domains]`
entries.details: Table | None | Maps host patterns to `allow` or `deny`. Rules apply only when the network proxy is active. The active proxy blocks domain requests if there are no `allow` entries, and deny entries override allow entries.

entries.name: `permissions.<name>.network.domains."<pattern>"`
entries.details: `allow` or `deny` | None | Supports exact hosts, `*.example.com` for subdomains, `**.example.com` for apex plus subdomains, and `*` as an allow-only global wildcard. Host patterns are normalized by trimming, lowercasing, stripping a trailing dot, and stripping simple ports or brackets.

entries.name: `[permissions.<name>.network.unix_sockets]`
entries.details: Table | None | Maps Unix socket allowlist overrides. Use only for local integrations such as Docker.

entries.name: `permissions.<name>.network.unix_sockets."<path>"`
entries.details: `allow` or `deny` | None | Adds an absolute Unix socket path to the effective allowlist with `allow`, or rejects it with `deny`. Denied entries are omitted from the effective allowlist.

entries.name: `permissions.<name>.network.proxy_url`
entries.details: URL string | `http://127.0.0.1:3128` | HTTP proxy listener used for `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, websocket proxy variables, and related tool proxy environment variables.

entries.name: `permissions.<name>.network.enable_socks5`
entries.details: Boolean | `true` | Enables the SOCKS5 listener used for `ALL_PROXY` and FTP proxy variables.

entries.name: `permissions.<name>.network.socks_url`
entries.details: URL string | `http://127.0.0.1:8081` | SOCKS5 listener address.

entries.name: `permissions.<name>.network.enable_socks5_udp`
entries.details: Boolean | `true` | Enables SOCKS5 UDP support when the SOCKS5 listener is enabled.

entries.name: `permissions.<name>.network.allow_upstream_proxy`
entries.details: Boolean | `true` | Allows the network sandbox proxy to respect upstream `HTTP(S)_PROXY` and `ALL_PROXY` settings for outbound requests.

entries.name: `permissions.<name>.network.allow_local_binding`
entries.details: Boolean | `false` | Disables the local/private-network guard when `true`. When `false`, exact local literals such as `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` must be explicitly allowlisted, and hostnames that resolve to local or private IPs remain blocked.

entries.name: `permissions.<name>.network.dangerously_allow_non_loopback_proxy`
entries.details: Boolean | `false` | Allows proxy listeners to bind non-loopback addresses. Leave unset for ordinary local development.

entries.name: `permissions.<name>.network.dangerously_allow_all_unix_sockets`
entries.details: Boolean | `false` | Bypasses the Unix socket allowlist where Unix socket proxying is supported. This is a broad local escape hatch.

entries.details: `autoUpdate`: whether to automatically download updated CLI versions; defaults to `true`.

entries.details: `banner`: frequency of showing animated banner; defaults to "once". - "always" displays it every time - "never" disables it - "once" displays it the first time

entries.name: bannerStyle
entries.details: `bannerStyle`: which artwork the startup banner uses; defaults to "mona". - "mona" is the two-Mona pixel-art hi-five - "classic" is the COPILOT wordmark with the goggled mascot - Ignored when `banner` resolves to "never"

entries.name: bashEnv
entries.details: `bashEnv`: whether to enable BASH_ENV support for bash shells; defaults to `false`. - Can also be set with --bash-env or --no-bash-env - Using either flag persists the preference to config

entries.name: beep
entries.details: `beep`: whether to beep when user attention is required; defaults to `false`.

entries.name: beepOnSchedule
entries.details: `beepOnSchedule`: whether to beep when a scheduled `/every` (or `/after`) run finishes; defaults to `true`. - Only applies when `beep` is enabled; set to `false` to silence completion beeps for scheduled runs.

entries.name: notifications
entries.details: `notifications`: whether to show OS notifications when user attention is required and when the agent finishes; defaults to `false`. - Set to `true` to enable desktop toasts. Toasts are suppressed while the terminal window already has focus. - Clicking a toast attempts to focus the terminal window that raised it where supported; multi-tab terminals (e.g. Windows Terminal) can't switch to the specific tab.

entries.name: powershellFlags
entries.details: `powershellFlags`: list of flags passed to PowerShell (pwsh) on startup; defaults to `["-NoProfile", "-NoLogo"]`. - Overrides the default flags when set; only applies on Windows - Examples: `["-NoProfile"]` to keep the logo, `[]` to load your profile and show the logo, `["-NoProfile", "-NoLogo", "-ExecutionPolicy", "Bypass"]` for locked-down environments - Use caution: flags that change execution semantics (`-Command`, `-File`, `-NoExit`, `-NonInteractive`, `-EncodedCommand`, `-InputFormat`, `-OutputFormat`) will break the runtime. See the settings documentation for details.

entries.name: compactPaste
entries.details: `compactPaste`: whether to collapse large pasted content into compact tokens; defaults to `true`. - When `true` (default), pastes with more than 10 lines are displayed as `[Paste #N - X lines]` - When `false`, all pasted content is displayed directly in the input

entries.name: copyOnSelect
entries.details: `copyOnSelect`: whether selecting text in alt screen mode automatically copies it to the system clipboard; defaults to `true` on macOS, `false` elsewhere. - When `true`, text is copied to the system clipboard as soon as the mouse button is released after a selection - When `false` (default), use Ctrl+C or right-click to copy selected text to the system clipboard - On Linux, the X11 primary selection is always updated on selection regardless of this setting

entries.name: commandHistoryMaxSize
entries.details: `commandHistoryMaxSize`: maximum number of recent prompts kept for Ctrl+R command-history search and up/down history navigation; defaults to `50`. - History is newest-first and deduplicated; entries beyond this many are dropped - Must be an integer between `1` and `1000`; out-of-range or invalid values fall back to `50` - Lowering it trims the in-memory history immediately and persists on the next submitted prompt

entries.name: customAgents.defaultLocalOnly
entries.details: `customAgents.defaultLocalOnly`: whether to default to only use local custom agents (no remote org/enterprise); defaults to `false`.

entries.name: deniedUrls
entries.details: `deniedUrls`: list of URLs or domains that are denied access. Denial rules take precedence over allow rules.

entries.name: proxyKerberosServicePrincipal
entries.details: `proxyKerberosServicePrincipal`: service principal name (SPN) for Kerberos/Negotiate proxy authentication; overrides the derived `HTTP/<proxy-host>`. Mirrors VS Code's `http.proxyKerberosServicePrincipal`. - The `COPILOT_PROXY_KERBEROS_SPN` environment variable, when set, takes precedence - Changing this requires a restart to take effect

entries.name: proxyUrl
entries.details: `proxyUrl`: proxy URL for HTTP(S) requests (e.g. `http://proxy.corp.example:3128`). - Can be overridden by the `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` environment variables (any casing, including lowercase `http_proxy` / `https_proxy`); if either is set in the environment, it takes precedence and this setting is ignored - `NO_PROXY` from the environment is still honored - Changing this requires a restart to take effect

entries.name: experimental
entries.details: `experimental`: whether to enable experimental features; defaults to `false`. - Can be enabled with --experimental flag, /settings experimental on, or /experimental (deprecated)

entries.name: memory
entries.details: `memory`: whether to enable agentic memory (cross-session fact recall); defaults to `true`. - Toggle with `/memory on|off` (writes this setting) - When `false`, the agent will not store or recall memories

entries.name: includeCoAuthoredBy
entries.details: `includeCoAuthoredBy`: whether to instruct the agent to add a Co-authored-by trailer to git commits; defaults to `true`.

entries.name: keepAlive
entries.details: `keepAlive`: keep-alive mode applied at CLI startup; prevents the system from sleeping while the session is active. Defaults to `"off"`. - `"off"` (default): system sleeps normally. - `"on"`: keep-alive is enabled for the duration of the session. - `"busy"`: keep-alive is enabled only while the agent is working on a turn. - Can also be set interactively with `/keep-alive [on|off|busy|<duration>]`.

entries.name: companyAnnouncements
entries.details: `companyAnnouncements`: list of messages to display in the banner on startup. - One message is randomly selected each time the CLI starts - Useful for team announcements or reminders

entries.name: continueOnAutoMode
entries.details: `continueOnAutoMode`: whether to automatically switch to auto mode when rate-limited; defaults to `false`. - When `true`, eligible rate limit errors (per-model, weekly, or integration limits) trigger an automatic switch to auto mode and retry - Does not apply to global rate limits, generic 429s, or BYOK providers

entries.name: stayInAutopilot
entries.details: `stayInAutopilot`: whether to stay in autopilot mode after an autopilot task completes; defaults to `true`. - When `true` (default), the CLI remains in autopilot mode after the agent calls `task_complete` instead of exiting to interactive mode - Set to `false` to revert to interactive mode after each completed task

entries.name: defaultMode
entries.details: `defaultMode`: agent mode new interactive sessions start in; defaults to "interactive". - One of "interactive", "plan", or "autopilot" - `--mode`, `--autopilot`, and `--plan` still win when passed - Resumed sessions keep their own persisted mode, and it does not apply to `-p`/`--prompt`, `--server`, or `--acp` runs

entries.name: defaultPermissionMode
entries.details: `defaultPermissionMode`: permission mode new interactive sessions start in; defaults to "manual". - `"manual"` (default): write and command requests are prompted; read-only requests are auto-approved - `"assisted"`: an LLM safety check auto-approves requests it judges safe and prompts otherwise; requires the experimental auto-approval feature, and is ignored when that feature is off or policy blocks auto-approval - `"allow-all"`: auto-approves everything, equivalent to launching with `--allow-all`; ignored when policy disables bypass-permissions mode - Any value is ignored on resumed sessions, outside interactive runs, and when `--allow-all`/`--yolo` already elevated the session - Pairs with `defaultMode: "autopilot"` to skip the autopilot permission confirmation entirely

entries.name: logLevel
entries.details: `logLevel`: log level for CLI; defaults to "default". Set to "all" for debug logging.

entries.name: model
entries.details: `model`: AI model to use for Copilot CLI; can be changed with /model command or --model flag option. - "claude-sonnet-5" - "claude-fable-5.1" - "claude-fable-5" - "claude-opus-5" - "claude-opus-4.8" - "claude-opus-4.8-fast" - "claude-opus-4.7" - "claude-sonnet-4.6" - "claude-haiku-4.5" - "gpt-5.6-sol" - "gpt-5.6-terra" - "gpt-5.6-luna" - "gpt-5.5" - "gpt-5.4"

entries.name: contextTier
entries.details: `contextTier`: context window tier for tiered-pricing models (e.g., "default" or "long_context"). - Can also be set with --context flag (overrides persisted setting) - Can be changed with /model command (context tier picker appears for eligible models)

entries.name: subagents.agents.<agent-name>
entries.details: `subagents.agents.<agent-name>`: per-subagent model, effortLevel, and contextTier selection. - Each field can be set to "inherit" to use the parent session's effective value - Configure interactively with the /subagents command

entries.name: mouse
entries.details: `mouse`: whether to enable mouse support in alt screen mode; defaults to `true`. - Can also be set with --mouse or --no-mouse - Using either flag persists the preference to config - When disabled, scroll wheel and click events are not captured by the CLI

entries.name: renderMarkdown
entries.details: `renderMarkdown`: whether to render markdown in the terminal; defaults to `true`.

entries.name: inlineImages
entries.details: `inlineImages`: whether to render images inline using the Kitty graphics protocol; defaults to `true`. - Requires the experimental `INLINE_IMAGES` feature (staff or experimental mode); otherwise image attachments show a text placeholder - Only takes effect on terminals that support Kitty graphics (e.g. Ghostty, kitty, WezTerm), and inside tmux with passthrough enabled - In a herdr pane, images are off by default: herdr draws them itself rather than passing them through, which additionally requires `experimental.kitty_graphics = true` in herdr's own config and cannot be detected from inside a pane. Set `COPILOT_INLINE_IMAGES_HERDR=1` to opt in once that setting is on - When disabled, image attachments show a text placeholder instead

entries.name: inlineImageLiveWindow
entries.details: `inlineImageLiveWindow`: maximum number of inline images kept resident in the terminal at once (the most-recent N by timeline order); defaults to `50`. - Images beyond N render as a text caption and have their data freed from the terminal, bounding its image memory in long, image-heavy sessions - Set to `0` to disable the cap (keep every inline image resident) - The `COPILOT_INLINE_IMAGE_LIMIT` environment variable overrides this setting

entries.name: scrollbar
entries.details: `scrollbar`: whether to show the scrollbar in scrollable views; defaults to `true`. - When `false`, the scrollbar is hidden and its gutter is reclaimed so content uses the full terminal width.

entries.name: respectGitignore
entries.details: `respectGitignore`: whether to exclude gitignored files from the `@` file mention picker; defaults to `true`. - When `false`, the `@` picker includes files that are normally excluded by `.gitignore` - Useful when sub-repositories or vendor directories are gitignored but still need to be referenced

entries.name: screenReader
entries.details: `screenReader`: whether to enable screen reader optimizations; defaults to `false`.

entries.name: showTipsOnStartup
entries.details: `showTipsOnStartup`: whether to show a random command tip when the CLI starts; defaults to `true`.

entries.name: stream
entries.details: `stream`: whether to enable streaming mode; defaults to `true`.

entries.name: streamerMode
entries.details: `streamerMode`: whether to enable streamer mode; defaults to `false`. - Hides preview model names and quota details (useful for streaming or screen sharing) - Toggle with the staff-only /streamer-mode command (persists across sessions) - Note: this setting is not exposed via /settings because /streamer-mode is staff-gated

entries.name: statusLine
entries.details: `statusLine`: configuration for a custom status line displayed below the input. - `type`: optional; when set, must be "command" - `command`: path to an executable script or a shell command that generates status line content. Supports `~` (home directory) and environment variables (`$HOME`, `${HOME}`, `${VAR:-default}`). Plain commands are run with the platform shell (`/bin/sh` on Unix-like systems, `cmd.exe` on Windows). The command receives the current session status as JSON on stdin and should print the status line to stdout. - `padding`: optional number of spaces to pad each line on the left - `refreshInterval`: optional integer number of seconds between command re-runs (minimum `1`, maximum `2147483`); omit to refresh only on events

entries.name: tabs
entries.details: `tabs`: configuration for the home screen navigation tab bar (Session, Agents, Issues, Pull requests, Gists). - `enabled`: whether to show the tab bar; defaults to `true`. Set to `false` to hide it entirely. - `sort`: array of tab identifiers controlling display order. Accepted identifiers (case-insensitive): `copilot` (Session), `agents`, `issues`, `pull-requests`, `gists`. Tabs not listed keep their default order after the listed ones; unknown identifiers are ignored. - `hide`: array of tab identifiers to hide (same identifiers as `sort`). Unknown identifiers are ignored; the `copilot` (Session) tab cannot be hidden.

entries.name: terminalProgress
entries.details: `terminalProgress`: whether to emit terminal progress indicators (OSC 9;4) while the agent is working; defaults to `true`. - Shows an indeterminate progress indicator in the terminal title bar or tab on supported emulators (Windows Terminal, iTerm2, Ghostty, ConEmu) - Set to `false` to suppress these escape sequences on terminals that render them as visible artifacts

entries.name: theme
entries.details: `theme`: color palette / theme for output; defaults to "github". - One of: "default", "github", "dim", "high-contrast", "colorblind" - Set via /settings theme <value>, or /theme <value> (deprecated) - `colorMode` is a legacy alias for `theme` and still works for now

entries.name: trustedFolders
entries.details: `trustedFolders`: list of folders where permission to read or execute files has been granted.

entries.name: updateTerminalTitle
entries.details: `updateTerminalTitle`: whether to update the terminal tab/window title with current intent; defaults to `true`. - Shows what the agent is currently working on in the terminal title bar - Only works on supported terminal emulators (xterm, iTerm, Windows Terminal, etc.) - Can also be disabled via the `COPILOT_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE` environment variable

entries.name: disableAllHooks

entries.name: hooks
